title: PixNerd: Pixel Neural Field Diffusion
claim: Our model generates diverse, high-fidelity, photorealistic samples across many categories and resolutions, showing its output quality at a glance.
layout: Mosaic grid: 4 large, 4 large, then 16 small tiles; no text
description: A dense mosaic of generated photographs with no text, arrows or labels. The top two rows hold eight large square tiles (4 per row) at the higher resolution. They show a golden retriever, a bald eagle, a white daisy, a spotted spaniel, an orange conch shell on a beach at sunset, a wolf spider, a pink flamingo head and a red newt. The bottom two rows hold sixteen smaller tiles (8 per row) at the lower resolution. They include a person holding a fish, a fire salamander, a circuit board, an iPod, a jellyfish, a hermit crab, a cruise ship, a van, a finch, a robin, a screen, a leather bag, a dolmen, a manhole cover, a harvester and an off-road jeep. The eye goes first to the large, vivid animal close-ups. The figure argues for sample quality and diversity through gallery density.
caption: Selected 256 × 256 and 512 × 512 resolution samples. Generated from PixNerd-XL/16 trained on ImageNet 256 × 256 resolution and ImageNet 512 × 512 resolution with CFG = 3.5.
abstract: The current success of diffusion transformers heavily depends on the compressed latent space shaped by the pre-trained variational autoencoder(VAE). However, this two-stage training paradigm inevitably introduces accumulated errors and decoding artifacts. To address the aforementioned problems, researchers return to pixel space at the cost of complicated cascade pipelines and increased token complexity. In contrast to their efforts, we propose to model the patch-wise decoding with neural field and present a single-scale, single-stage, efficient, end-to-end solution, coined as pixel neural field diffusion~(PixelNerd). Thanks to the efficient neural field representation in PixNerd, we directly achieved 2.15 FID on ImageNet $256\times256$ and 2.84 FID on ImageNet $512\times512$ without any complex cascade pipeline or VAE. We also extend our PixNerd framework to text-to-image applications. Our PixNerd-XXL/16 achieved a competitive 0.73 overall score on the GenEval benchmark and 80.9 overall score on the DPG benchmark.
